title: Dynamic MIG slice affinity: real-time clock steering and attention kernel pairing
text:
Dynamic MIG slice affinity: real-time clock steering and attention kernel pairing

description:
Improve end-to-end latency and throughput for mixed short/long-context workloads on multi-tenant GPU servers by dynamically assigning requests to MIG slices and steering GPU clocks while selecting the optimal attention kernel variant at prefill time. This ticket covers design, prototype, benchmarks, and an initial canary rollout for H100/L40S/A10 hosts.

background:
We observe regressions for mixed workloads when static MIG partitions or fixed clock policies are used: short queries get batched with long contexts, inflating latency; aggressive clocks increase thermal events; kernel selection at decode often mismatches prefill characteristics.
Existing work (ENG-33102, ENG-35892) provided kernel packetizers and profile-driven scheduling but lacks a tight feedback loop between MIG slice affinity, real-time clock steering, and attention-kernel pairing.
Goal is to reduce p95/p99 latency for 1-8 token responses by 20% on H100 and L40S while keeping cost per token stable for long-context workloads on A10 clusters.
This intersects infra (daemon for clock control), runtime (kernel chooser and prefill analyzer), and autoscaler policies (to avoid noisy-neighbor saturation on slices).

proposal:
Implement a runtime hook that runs at request admission and prefill that: (a) samples short histogram metrics (tokens, prompt length distribution), (b) consults a slice-affinity table to pick a preferred MIG slice class (small/medium/large), and (c) picks a candidate attention kernel variant (fused/tiling/wave-optimized) based on profile.
Introduce a clock-steering agent on hosts to adjust GPU clocks in 3 tiers: conserve, balanced, performance. Runtime signals request mix and desired tier; agent enforces limits with safety timers to avoid rapid changes.
Add a fallback policy: if preferred slice is overloaded or clock change blocked, select a compatible kernel that preserves latency SLOs and optionally route to spare capacity or burst pool.
Collect telemetry hooks (per-request tags) to attribute latency/cost to slice, clock tier, and kernel variant for analysis and automated regressions detection.
Prototype on H100 first (because of NVLink/thermal behavior), then validate on L40S and A10 with adjusted clock delta tables.
Provide a canary rollout via console: model-route flag to enable dynamic affinity for a small percentage of traffic with automatic rollback on p99 degradation > 10%.
Deliver a runtime-1.22 feature gate and an ops runbook for on-call and SRE to operate clock agent and revert changes.

design_decisions:
Prefer coarse-grained, safety-timed clock transitions (>= 30s hold) to avoid oscillation across rapid workload shifts.
Keep kernel selection deterministic per request fingerprint to maximize cache/KV reuse; use a short-lived ephemeral cache for kernel profiles.
Use a light-weight admission sampler (5-10% of requests) for continuous profiling; full routing uses exponentially-weighted estimates to avoid noisy decisions.
Prioritize latency SLOs for short-response endpoints and throughput/cost for long-response batch endpoints; map these policies to different MIG slice classes.
Host-level clock agent runs as non-root with limited power control capabilities via nvml and cgroups where supported; fall back to conservative policy if control not available.

tradeoffs:
Pros: reduces token latency for short queries, better thermal/power utilization, and tighter cost/latency control across mixed workloads.
Cons: added complexity in runtime scheduling, potential safety concerns around frequent clock changes, increased operability burden for SRE.
Risk of suboptimal kernel pairing for rare model architectures—mitigated by a conservative default kernel and offline ML model to predict pairings over time.
MIG slice affinity can reduce isolation for tenants if slices are mis-sized; we will default to tenant-configurable hard limits.

acceptance_criteria:
p95 for short-response workload (<= 8 tokens) improved by >= 15% on H100 compared to baseline under mixed load
p99 regression < 5% for long-context workloads on A10 under same traffic mix
Clock agent does not flip tiers more frequently than once per 30s in steady-state tests
Canary can be disabled from Console and fully rolled back without residual host state in <= 5 minutes
End-to-end telemetry surfaces slice, clock-tier, kernel-variant for >95% of sampled requests

benchmark_plan:
Use existing perf harness: mixed_short_long_v2 with ratios 70/30, 50/50, 30/70.
Run runs across H100 (MIG enabled, slices small/med/large), L40S, and A10 with default clocks and with dynamic clock steering enabled.
Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU power draw, frequency stability, and thermal trip events.
Compare cost-per-token estimates using runtime billing sim harness to ensure no >10% increase in unit cost for long workloads.

rollout_plan:
Stage 1: internal canary on infra-owned clusters (5% traffic) for 48h; collect telemetry and run regressions.
Stage 2: controlled customer canary for non-SLAed routes (10% traffic) for 72h.
Stage 3: broader rollout to H100 fleet with gradual ramp and circuit breaker on p99 regressions.
Stage 4: enable for L40S/A10 after hardware-specific tuning and two successful H100 waves.

monitoring_and_rollback:
Create console dashboard showing slice utilization, clock-tier distribution, kernel-variant counts, and per-route p99.
Auto-roll back if p99 increases by >10% for 30m or if thermal trip events spike >2x baseline on a host group.
Manual rollback steps documented in runbook; host agent has 'freeze' mode that rejects external clock changes during rollback.

notes:
Feasibility meeting 2026-02-18: ops expressed concern about nvml availability on some cloud partners; added fallback conservative policy.
Discussed kernel deterministic mapping with Research; decided to fingerprint by model name + avg prompt length bucket.
We should coordinate with Sales for customers using dedicated capacity; present in upcoming dedicated-customer sync.
